_README: Curated allowlist for scripts/validate_docs_reality.py. Two CLI buckets: roadmap_allow (intentional forward-looking / other-product / internal-tool references — NEVER a failure, so this bucket is a PERMANENT MUTE: put a reference here only when the command is genuinely someone else's surface, and name where that surface lives) and tracked_drift (KNOWN drift in customer docs/marketing being removed/reconciled by in-flight docs PRs — non-fatal in the normal gate so a green tree stays green, but FAILS under --strict; this is the punch-list). Any `corelink <cmd>` that is neither valid, roadmap-allowed, nor tracked FAILS the gate — that is how NEW drift is caught.
_RULES_FOR_NEW_ENTRIES: 1. A stale entry is NOT harmless. It is a permanent mute that re-silences the same defect the day it recurs — that is exactly how `corelink ping` survived in the served install script for months while the gate printed `0 drift`. The validator now emits a `[suppression-hygiene] ... never matched` WARN for every entry that matches nothing; drive that list to zero.

2. Before adding an entry, answer IN THE REASON: is the DOC wrong, or is the PRODUCT wrong? If a customer is told to run a command that would give them a working capability and the CLI simply does not have it, that is a PRODUCT gap — say so, and link the tracking issue. Do not file it as a wording fix.

3. Before adding an entry, check whether the same phantom command also ships in an EXECUTABLE surface the gate cannot see (apps/get-corelink-worker/src/install.ts, *.sh, e2e tests, workflows, the repo-root README/ROADMAP). The gate scans only .md/.mdx/.mdc/.html/.txt under apps/docs/{docs,blog,src}, marketing/ and docs/ (minus docs/knowledge, docs/okf-wiki-site, docs/internal). Suppressing the doc echo of a defect that also ships in code is the worst outcome this file can produce.

4. New entries SHOULD carry provenance: `added` (ISO date), `owner`, `expires` (ISO date), `ref` (PR/issue). The existing entries carry none — there is no way to tell `known and accepted` from `known and forgotten`.

grounding.marker: The edge TLS floor for `humangr.com` is **1.2**

deferred_coherence.reason: The humangr.com edge floor is TLS 1.2, not 1.3 — lowered 2026-07-19 so native-tls/SecureTransport clients (sccache) could complete a handshake (ADR-0072). A customer-facing or regulator-facing document that says 1.3 is enforced/minimum overstates a security control that a prospect can disprove with one scan. Say 'TLS 1.2 floor, 1.3 negotiated'. Outbound calls to third parties (Stripe, KMS, Clerk) legitimately negotiate 1.3 and are allowed.

hostname._README: Registry for [hostname-liveness] in scripts/validate_docs_reality.py. `live_allow` is a FACT REGISTRY, not a mute: every entry was verified to resolve AND serve on the date in its reason (re-derive with `python3 scripts/validate_docs_reality.py --verify-dns`). `live_patterns` covers name FAMILIES that are infrastructure records rather than enumerable hosts (DKIM selectors). `tracked_dead` is the SUPPRESSION bucket: non-fatal in the normal gate, FAILS under --strict, and every entry MUST carry a reason, an owner and an ISO `expires` — a missing or past expiry is a hard failure, because an expiring suppression that never expires is a permanent mute wearing a date. Any *.humangr.com hostname on a shipped surface that is in neither bucket FAILS.
_REFRESH_RECIPE: The gate NEVER touches the network: CI here runs on the founder's own Mac, and a DNS-dependent gate is a flaky gate that trains everyone to re-run it.

To refresh: `python3 scripts/validate_docs_reality.py --verify-dns` (opt-in, networked). It probes every hostname found on a shipped surface plus every allowlisted one, with DNS resolution + a TLS handshake on :443.
LIVE  -> belongs in live_allow, with the probe date in the reason string.
DEAD / DNS-ONLY -> fix the DOCS (preferred) or add a tracked_dead entry. Do NOT add it to live_allow: that bucket asserts the host exists.
`python3 scripts/validate_docs_reality.py --list-hosts` dumps the current corpus with per-host verdicts and mention counts.

live_patterns.reason: DKIM selector records. A family of TXT records, not an enumerable set of serving hosts — pattern-allowed rather than listed one by one.

status.corelink.humangr.com.reason: DNS RESOLVES but the TLS handshake fails, so no client can reach it — a dead host that looks alive to a `dig`. It is a THIRD-level name, and Cloudflare Universal SSL covers `humangr.com` and `*.humangr.com` ONE LEVEL ONLY, so the edge holds no certificate for it; BetterUptime returns 403 for that Host, meaning the custom domain was never registered on their side either. Neither side holds a certificate. The fix requires the BetterUptime dashboard (register the custom domain, then issue the cert) and is tracked separately by the tech lead — it cannot be done from this repo, which is why this is a suppression with an expiry rather than a docs edit.
